rationale: All three lenses ran on the full diff. The narrow try/except McpError around session.call_tool converts downstream JSON-RPC protocol errors into a 200 isError CallToolResult, resolving the ticket's generic-500 root cause; timeouts/connection/httpx-auth errors (not McpError on the client path) still propagate, and existing 401/403/404/503/504 tests are unaffected. Acceptance audit: all 6 criteria pass. Commit format complies with git-workflow.md; error.data is deliberately withheld while code+message are surfaced (criterion f). The edge-case lens's critical UrlElicitationRequiredError finding was verified as a non-regression: the client-side send_request raises only base McpError (never the subclass), this service uses no elicitation, and the prior behavior was a 500 regardless. Dismissed 4 findings (theoretical exc.error null-safety x2 merged, over-broad-catch, low-confidence httpx-wrap, and the elicitation-subclass concern). Deferred 3 non-blocking hardening ideas (severity-based log level; masking/truncating the downstream error.message before logging and surfacing; response-text length cap) for a follow-up if telemetry shows leaky downstream servers.

Warning log carries code+message server-side; caller sees code+message only; error.data withheld.
